problems.quote: “approve” and “acknowledge” are positive polarity verbs that become infelicitous under negation
problems.problem: The verbs “approve” and “acknowledge” are not positive polarity items (PPIs); they can be freely negated (e.g., “did not approve” is perfectly natural). True PPIs include “some”, “already”, “rather”. The examples “welcome”, “embrace” are also not PPIs.
problems.correction: “approve” and “acknowledge” are not PPIs; they negate freely. True PPIs (e.g., “some”) resist negation; NPIs (e.g., “budge”) require it.
problems.verifierReason: Original falsely claims 'approve'/'acknowledge' are PPIs; they negate freely. Correction correctly identifies true PPIs (e.g., 'some') and NPIs.

problems.quote: Options like “proof” or “confirmation” are positive polarity and create a semantic clash because “no proof” is acceptable but “no confirmation” is less idiomatic
problems.problem: Nouns such as “proof” and “confirmation” are not positive polarity items; “no confirmation” is fully idiomatic in formal audit language. Polarity sensitivity applies to determiners/adverbs (e.g., “any”, “ever”), not to these nouns.
problems.correction: Nouns like “proof” and “confirmation” are not polarity-sensitive; both “no proof” and “no confirmation” are idiomatic.
problems.verifierReason: Original falsely treats 'proof'/'confirmation' as polarity-sensitive nouns; both 'no proof' and 'no confirmation' are fully idiomatic.

problems.quote: the latter means “no bank did”
problems.problem: “Every bank did not ______ the guideline” does not unambiguously mean “no bank did”; in English it is scopally ambiguous and often conveys “not every bank did” (partial negation).
problems.correction: “Every bank did not …” is ambiguous and often means “not every bank did”, not “no bank did”.
problems.verifierReason: Original claims 'Every bank did not' unambiguously means 'no bank did'; it is scopally ambiguous, often meaning 'not every bank did'.

problems.quote: licensing “yield” and “benefit” as NPIs
problems.problem: “yield” and “benefit” are not negative polarity items; the NPI in the example is “any”. The matrix predicate “doubts” licenses the NPI “any”, not the verb “yield” or the noun “benefit”.
problems.correction: licensing the NPI “any” with a verb like “yield” and a noun like “benefit”
problems.verifierReason: Original misidentifies 'yield'/'benefit' as NPIs; the NPI is 'any', licensed by 'doubts'. Correction accurately rephrases.

problems.quote: “provide” (will provide liquidity) changes the transitivity pattern and breaks the ellipsis licence
problems.problem: Both “cut” and “provide” are transitive verbs taking a direct object (“rates”, “liquidity”); “provide” does not alter the transitivity pattern and does not break the ellipsis licence.
problems.correction: “provide” (will provide liquidity) is also transitive and maintains the ellipsis licence.
problems.verifierReason: Original claims 'provide' changes transitivity and breaks ellipsis; both 'cut' and 'provide' are transitive, so ellipsis is maintained.

problems.quote: at a given temperature, all gases have the same average molecular kinetic energy, (3/2)kT per molecule for monatomic gases
problems.problem: The average molecular kinetic energy is not the same for all gases; only the translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)kT for all ideal gases. The value (3/2)kT is the total kinetic energy only for monatomic gases.
problems.correction: at a given temperature, all ideal gases have the same average translational kinetic energy, (3/2)kT per molecule
problems.verifierReason: Original conflates total KE with translational KE; only translational KE is (3/2)kT for all ideal gases.
